payload.title: Wedding RSVP Website Guide to Collect Every Reply
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s, about a year out from a destination wedding with 60 to 120 guests (many flying in, some from other countries and time zones), who know they want replies collected online and now need to choose what kind of RSVP tool fits a weekend of events, travel and accommodation questions, without paying for features they will not use.
payload.goal: Book a Wedded Concierge consultation with a Wedded Advisor (one CTA, via /wonderland-concierge with UTM tags).
payload.angle: Page one compares named platforms and tells couples which brand to sign up to. We compare the five kinds of RSVP website instead (all-in-one wedding website, stand-alone RSVP or form tool, invitation platform with RSVP built in, a planning app with RSVP, DIY form plus spreadsheet), judged on what a destination weekend actually needs: one reply that covers the welcome dinner, the wedding and the day-after brunch, travel and arrival questions that feed room blocks, and guests replying from other time zones and languages. It also turns the no-cost versus paid tier question into a short list of checks a couple can run on any tool, so the advice stays true when plans and pricing change.
must_include: What an RSVP website does (live yes/no/awaiting, per-person meal and dietary fields, plus-one names, timestamps) and when a stand-alone RSVP form beats building a full wedding website (e.g. you already have a site, or you only need replies).

The five kinds compared, with NO platform names: (1) all-in-one wedding website with RSVP, (2) stand-alone RSVP or form tool, (3) invitation platform with RSVP built in, (4) a planning app with RSVP, where Wonderland Studio appears only as 'our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs' with no feature counts, tiers or prices, (5) DIY form plus spreadsheet. Include a features and trade-offs table (rows such as multi-event RSVP, custom questions, guest login needed or not, reminders, export, QR codes, privacy controls, effort to set up) with no prices.

What changes between no-cost and paid tiers, written as questions to check on any tool (e.g. guest or event limits, custom questions, removing the tool's branding, custom domain, password protection, reminder sends, data export, ads shown to guests). No prices and never the word 'free' (use 'no-cost tier' or 'at no cost').

Destination features section: travel and accommodation questions, arrival and departure dates, multi-event RSVP for welcome dinner, wedding and day-after brunch, plus-ones and children, meal and dietary needs per person, time zones (deadline stated with a date and time zone) and languages for overseas family.
QR codes on invitations and save-the-dates, with the plain URL printed underneath as a fallback.

Privacy of guest details (what you collect, who can see it, password protection, deleting data after the wedding), with an official source cited at the claim (e.g. OAIC guidance) and [[VERIFY]] on any statement about what the law requires of a private couple.

Deadlines and chasing replies only as links, no duplicated guidance: /wedding-invitations-when-should-we-make-our-rsvp-date (deadline) and /how-to-manage-wedding-rsvps (process; note it resolves to /expert-advice/wedding-rsvp, so link the final URL). Also link /expert-advice/wedding-website for what else goes on the site.

FAQ (4 to 6 questions on choosing a type, e.g. 'Do guests need an account to RSVP?', 'Can one RSVP cover several events?', 'Should we use a stand-alone RSVP tool if we already have a wedding website?', 'What should we check before paying for an upgrade?'). No deadline or platform questions.

Close with one Wedded Advisor line taken from brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30, e.g. 'One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact' or 'Guest room blocks held by the advisor, with Wedded Privileges on every room', linking the Concierge CTA.
avoid: Any platform or competitor name (drop Zola, The Knot, Joy, Minted, RSVPify, Riley & Grey and any other).
Any price, cost figure or tier price; the word 'free' anywhere (body, table, FAQ, headings, alt text, meta).
Statistics or numeric claims about guest behaviour (e.g. reply rates, 'skews older', 'now the norm').
Research talk ('we verified', 'feature claims verified 27 Aug 2026', 'according to SERPs').
Deadline timings, reminder schedules or chasing scripts (owned by the RSVP date page and the manage RSVPs page).
Wonderland Studio feature claims beyond 'planning app for seating charts and RSVPs' (no 'four ways to invite', 'one reply moves four things', 'eleven planning tools', registry statements).
Brand-facts step 3 wording that contains 'free' ('actually free when you want them').
Generic 'what to put on a wedding website' content (owned by /expert-advice/wedding-website).
